claim: The gut contractile organoid was derived from the muscle layer of chicken embryonic hindgut.
source: We here developed a novel contractile organoid that is derived from the muscle layer of chicken embryonic hindgut.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the source tissue for the organoid in the abstract.

claim: The gut contractile organoid contained smooth muscle cells (SMCs) and interstitial cells of Cajal (ICCs) with few enteric neurons.
source: The organoid contained smooth muscle cells (SMCs) and interstitial cells of Cajal (ICCs; pacemaker) with few enteric neurons and underwent periodic contractions.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes the cellular composition of the organoid.

claim: The gut contractile organoid underwent periodic contractions.
source: The organoid contained smooth muscle cells (SMCs) and interstitial cells of Cajal (ICCs; pacemaker) with few enteric neurons and underwent periodic contractions.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that the organoid underwent periodic contractions.

claim: The organoid was formed by self-organization with morphological arrangements of ICCs (internal) and SMCs (peripheral).
source: The organoid was formed by self-organization with morphological arrangements of ICCs (internal) and SMCs (peripheral), allowing identification of these cells in live.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes the self-organization and spatial arrangement of cell types.

claim: Ca2+ transients between ICC-ICC, SMC-SMC, or SMC-ICC were markedly coordinated.
source: GCaMP-Ca2+ imaging analyses revealed that Ca2+ transients between ICC-ICC, SMC-SMC, or SMC-ICC were markedly coordinated.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the coordination of Ca2+ transients based on GCaMP imaging.

claim: Gap junctions play a role in ICC-to-SMC signaling.
source: Pharmacological studies further suggested a role of gap junctions in ICC-to-SMC signaling, and also possible mechanical feedback from SMC's contraction to ICC's pace-making activities.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that pharmacological studies suggested a role for gap junctions.

claim: There is possible mechanical feedback from SMC's contraction to ICC's pace-making activities.
source: Pharmacological studies further suggested a role of gap junctions in ICC-to-SMC signaling, and also possible mechanical feedback from SMC's contraction to ICC's pace-making activities.
evidence: The abstract explicitly mentions possible mechanical feedback based on pharmacological studies.

claim: Two organoids with different rhythms became synchronized when mediated by SMCs.
source: In addition, two organoids with different rhythms became synchronized when mediated by SMCs, unveiling a novel contribution of SMCs to ICC's pace-making.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes the synchronization of two organoids mediated by SMCs.

claim: Gut peristaltic movements are achieved by intricate regulations of intercellular functions among multiple cell types.
source: The gut peristaltic movements are achieved by intricate regulations of intercellular functions among multiple cell types.
evidence: The introduction explicitly states this as established knowledge.

claim: The embryonic gut undergoes peristaltic movements even without experience of food intake.
source: It is known in vertebrates that the embryonic gut undergoes peristaltic movements even without experience of food intake.
evidence: The introduction explicitly states this as known fact in vertebrates.

claim: Sites of OPW are randomly distributed along the gut axis at early stages and later become confined to specific sites.
source: We have recently reported using chicken embryos that sites of OPW are randomly distributed along the gut axis at early stages, and they later become confined to specific sites, and that this confinement of OPWs enables rhythmic and patterned peristaltic movements (Shikaya et al., 2022).
evidence: The introduction cites a previous study by the authors.

claim: Enteric nervous system (ENS), SMCs, and interstitial cells of Cajal (ICCs) play important roles in peristaltic movements.
source: In a long history of gut motility studies, it has been known that enteric nervous system (ENS), SMCs, and interstitial cells of Cajal (ICCs) play important roles in peristaltic movements (Barajas-López et al., 1989; Camborová et al., 2003; Chevalier et al., 2020; Huizinga et al., 1995; Kito et al., 2005; Liu et al., 1998; Rumessen and Thuneberg, 1996; Sanders et al., 1991; Takaki, 2003; Takayama et al., 2002; Thomsen et al., 1998).
evidence: The introduction cites multiple studies supporting this claim.

claim: At early embryonic stages, gut movement/peristalsis does not require ENS activity.
source: It has widely been accepted that: (1) at early embryonic stages, gut movement/peristalsis does not require ENS activity
evidence: The introduction states this as widely accepted knowledge.

claim: ICCs serve as a pacemaker dictating their rhythm to SMCs.
source: It has widely been accepted that: (1) at early embryonic stages, gut movement/peristalsis does not require ENS activity, (2) ICCs serve as a pacemaker dictating their rhythm to SMCs
evidence: The introduction states this as widely accepted knowledge.

claim: The contraction is executed by SMC and not by ICCs, since thick fibers of myosin are found solely in SMCs.
source: (3) the contraction is executed by SMC and not by ICCs, since thick fibers of myosin are found solely in SMCs.
evidence: The introduction states this as widely accepted knowledge with a structural basis.

claim: Slow waves occur spontaneously in ICCs but not in SMCs.
source: A series of elaborate electrophysiological studies showed that slow waves (a type of changes in membrane potential characteristic of gut movements) occur spontaneously in ICCs but not in SMCs
evidence: The introduction cites electrophysiological studies supporting this claim.

claim: Slow waves lead to voltage-dependent Ca2+ influx evoking action potential, which is transmitted to SMCs to execute gut contraction in register with ICC's pace-making rhythm.
source: and that these slow waves lead to voltage-dependent Ca2+ influx evoking action potential, which is somehow transmitted to SMCs to execute gut contraction in register with ICC's pace-making rhythm (Baker et al., 2021; Torihashi et al., 2002).
evidence: The introduction cites studies supporting this mechanism.

claim: c-Kit-deficient mouse mutants (W/Wv) have severely affected ICC differentiation leading to a failure of gut peristalsis.
source: The knowledge that ICCs act as a pacemaker was supported by compelling evidence obtained by c-Kit-deficient mouse mutants (W/Wv), in which ICC differentiation was severely affected leading to a failure of gut peristalsis (Huizinga et al., 1995; Torihashi et al., 1999).
evidence: The introduction cites studies on c-Kit-deficient mutants.

claim: Differentiation states of mouse hindgut-derived cells were successfully maintained for a relatively long period of time in a serum-free culture medium.
source: Recently, it was reported that differentiation states of mouse hindgut-derived cells were successfully maintained for a relatively long period of time in a serum-free culture medium (Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: The introduction cites a study on mouse hindgut-derived cell culture.

claim: When cultured in DMEM/Ham's F-12 or Ham's F-12, dissociated cells formed very small aggregates containing several cells at day 1, the morphology of which did not change significantly until day 5.
source: When cultured in DMEM/Ham's F-12 or Ham's F-12, dissociated cells formed very small aggregates containing several cells at day 1, the morphology of which did not change significantly until day 5 (Figure 1A).
evidence: The results section describes observations from culture experiments shown in Figure 1A.

claim: When cultured in the Neurobasal medium, cells formed clusters that were interconnected by elongated cells with neighboring clusters as early as day 1.
source: In clear contrast, when cultured in the Neurobasal medium, cells formed clusters that were interconnected by elongated cells with neighboring clusters as early as day 1.
evidence: The results section describes observations from culture experiments.

claim: Clusters grew as larger aggregates by day 3 and became spherical by day 5 in Neurobasal medium.
source: These clusters grew as larger aggregates by day 3 and became spherical by day 5.
evidence: The results section describes temporal progression of cluster formation.

claim: Poly-Lysine or collagen substrates with Neurobasal medium did not yield spheroid formation.
source: We also tested different substrates, Poly-Lysine or collagen for dish coating with the Neurobasal medium, but neither one yielded spheroid.
evidence: The results section describes negative results from substrate testing.

claim: The spheroids underwent reiterative contractions at day 3, and these contractions were observed at least until day 7 of culture.
source: The spheroids underwent reiterative contractions at day 3, and these contractions were observed at least until day 7 of culture (Figure 2A for normalized intensities of three representative organoids for each stage, Figure 2—video 1).
evidence: The results section describes contraction observations with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: Interval periods between two successive peaks were 13.3 s, 15.4 s and 19.6 s for cultures at day 3, day 5, and day 7, respectively (median values).
source: Time-lapse imaging of the contractions combined with quantitative assessments by MATLAB (MathWorks, see Materials and methods) showed that interval periods between two successive peaks were 13.3 s, 15.4 s and 19.6 s for cultures at day 3, day 5, and day 7, respectively (median values; Figure 2B; contraction intervals).
evidence: The results section provides quantitative measurements of contraction intervals.

claim: At day 3, c-Kit+/αSMA- signals were detected in the internal region, and c-Kit+/αSMA+ signals at the periphery.
source: In the clusters at day 3, c-Kit+/αSMA- signals were detected in the internal region, and c-Kit+/αSMA+ signals at the periphery (Figure 3A, Day 3)
evidence: The results section describes immunostaining results shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Internal cells at day 3 were differentiated ICCs, whereas peripheral cells were ICC/SMC progenitors.
source: suggesting that internal cells were differentiated ICCs, whereas peripheral cells were ICC/SMC progenitors.
evidence: The results section provides interpretation of immunostaining data based on marker expression.

claim: At day 5 onward, c-Kit+/αSMA- cells and c-Kit-/αSMA+ cells were segregated, which were located internally and peripherally, respectively.
source: At day 5 onward, c-Kit+/αSMA- cells and c-Kit-/αSMA+ cells were segregated, which were located internally and peripherally, respectively (Figure 3A, Day 5)
evidence: The results section describes immunostaining results at day 5.

claim: The spatial segregation of ICCs and SMCs remained unchanged until day 7.
source: and this spatial segregation of the cells remained unchanged until day 7 (Figure 3A, Day 7), the latest stage examined in this study.
evidence: The results section describes temporal stability of cell organization.

claim: The peripherally lining cells were positive for desmin staining, supporting that these cells were SMCs.
source: The peripherally lining cells were also positive for desmin staining, supporting that these cells were SMCs (Figure 3B).
evidence: The results section describes desmin staining results shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Infection with RCAS-GapEGFP into a forming spheroid visualized multipolar ICCs in the internal region.
source: Infection with RCAS-GapEGFP into a forming spheroid further visualized multipolar ICCs in the internal region (Figure 3C), a morphology known to be characteristic of ICC-MY which would normally reside in the layer of myenteric plexus (Mei et al., 2009; Sanders et al., 2014).
evidence: The results section describes visualization of ICC morphology with reference to literature.

claim: ICCs of a different type were elongated, thin, and lining underneath the peripheral SMCs, possibly ICC-IM.
source: ICCs of a different type were also recognized, which were elongated, thin, and lining underneath the peripheral SMCs (Figure 3A, Day 7). It is possible that these were ICC-IM, known to be embedded in and tightly associated with smooth muscles in the gut (Huizinga et al., 2011; Iino and Horiguchi, 2006).
evidence: The results section describes ICC morphology with speculative identification based on literature.

claim: The spheroid contained few neural cells (ENS), if any, revealed by anti-Tuj1 antibody.
source: Unexpectedly, the spheroid contained few neural cells (ENS), if any, revealed by anti-Tuj1 antibody (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The results section describes immunostaining results for neural markers.

claim: When tetrodotoxin was added to culture medium, contraction intervals of organoids were comparable to those of control.
source: Indeed, when tetrodotoxin was added to culture medium, contraction intervals of organoids were comparable to those of control (before the administration) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), confirming little contribution by ENS.
evidence: The results section describes pharmacological experiment results.

claim: The proportion of SMCs was smaller than that of ICCs in the organoid, contrasting with the intact gut.
source: We counted cell numbers of each cell type per organoid and found that, contrasting with the intact gut, the proportion of SMCs was smaller than that of ICCs (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), possibly due to a cell-type-specific loss during culture preparation.
evidence: The results section describes cell counting results with speculation about the cause.

claim: N-cadherin signals were seen in the internal ICCs, and not in the peripheral SMCs.
source: N-cadherin signals were seen in the internal ICCs, and not in the peripheral SMCs (Figure 3D).
evidence: The results section describes N-cadherin staining results.

claim: N-cadherin plays a role in the segregation of ICCs and SMCs.
source: Thus, it is likely that N-cadherin plays a role in the segregation.
evidence: The results section provides inference based on N-cadherin expression pattern.

claim: The oscillatory rhythm of Ca2+ transients as a whole organoid was highly concomitant with that of contractions.
source: As expected, the oscillatory rhythm of Ca2+ transients as a whole organoid was highly concomitant with that of contractions (Figure 4B, Figure 4—video 1).
evidence: The results section describes correlation between Ca2+ transients and contractions.

claim: Three ROIs in the SMC layer exhibited a synchronous pattern of Ca2+ oscillations.
source: We set up 3 regions of interest (ROIs) in the SMC layer with one ROI corresponding to one cell and captured the Ca2+ transients. The three ROIs exhibited a synchronous pattern of Ca2+ oscillations (Figure 4C, SMCs).
evidence: The results section describes Ca2+ imaging results for SMCs.

claim: Ca2+ oscillations in three ROIs in the central region (ICCs) were synchronous.
source: Similarly, Ca2+ oscillations in three ROIs in the central region (ICCs) were synchronous (Figure 4C, ICCs).
evidence: The results section describes Ca2+ imaging results for ICCs.

claim: The Ca2+ rhythm was synchronized between ICC and SMC.
source: We further compared Ca2+ oscillations between ICC-SMC by setting up one ROI in each of ICC and SMC. Again, the Ca2+ rhythm was synchronized between these heterotypic cell types (Figure 4C, ICC/SMC).
evidence: The results section describes Ca2+ imaging results for ICC-SMC pairs.

claim: A peak of Ca2+ transient in ICC preceded that in SMC with a time lag (latency) of 700 ms on average.
source: With a deeper scrutinization, a peak of Ca2+ transient in ICC preceded that in SMC with a time lag (also called latency) of 700 ms on average (Figure 4C, ICC/SMC; Figure 4D, 104 peaks for 14 organoids)
evidence: The results section provides quantitative measurement of temporal relationship between ICC and SMC Ca2+ peaks.

claim: 100 μM concentrations of CBX or 18β-GA showed no detectable effects on the recurring contractions of an organoid.
source: Contrary to our expectation, none of the 100 μM concentrations of CBX or 18β-GA showed detectable effects on the recurring contractions of an organoid with frequency/interval comparable to the control (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B, Figure 5—video 2).
evidence: The results section describes pharmacological experiment results.

claim: The drug administration at day 3 also yielded undetectable effects assessed at day 7.
source: These undetectable effects were not due to insufficient penetrance of the drugs into the organoid, since the drug administration at day 3, when organoid-forming cells were still at 2D in culture, also yielded undetectable effects assessed at day 7 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The results section describes control experiment results.

claim: Overall synchronization was retained between ICCs and SMCs after gap junction inhibitor treatment, but the preceding peak of Ca2+ transient in ICC was abolished.
source: With a closer look, however, while overall synchronization was retained between ICCs and SMCs, the preceding peak of Ca2+ transient in ICC was abolished (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: The results section describes detailed analysis of Ca2+ dynamics after drug treatment.

claim: Gap junctions are required for ICC-to-SMC signals, at least partly.
source: Collectively, while the contribution by gap junctions to the periodic contraction and intercellular synchronization in the Day 7 organoid is relatively limited, the ICC-to-SMC signals require gap junction-mediated communications, at least partly.
evidence: The results section provides interpretation of pharmacological experiment results.

claim: Blebbistatin ceased periodic contractions of organoids in a concentration-dependent manner.
source: We found that blebbistatin ceased periodic contractions of organoids in a concentration-dependent manner: while intervals were shorter with smaller amplitude at 5 μM, contractions were ceased completely at 10 μM (Figure 6A and B, Figure 6—video 1).
evidence: The results section describes dose-dependent effects of blebbistatin.

claim: The 10 μM blebbistatin-treated specimens resumed contractions following medium washout.
source: The 10 μM-treated specimens resumed contractions following medium washout, showing that the organoids were alive (Figure 6B).
evidence: The results section describes reversibility of blebbistatin effects.

claim: Blebbistatin extinguished periodic Ca2+ transients in both SMCs and ICCs.
source: Markedly, periodic Ca2+ transients were extinguished not only in SMCs but also in ICCs, yielding no/little synchronous Ca2+ patterns among and between ICCs and SMCs (Figure 6C–F).
evidence: The results section describes Ca2+ imaging results after blebbistatin treatment.

claim: The contractility feeds back to ICCs to generate/maintain their periodic rhythm.
source: Although a possible direct inhibition of non-muscle myosin II in ICCs cannot be excluded, these findings raised an interesting possibility that the contractility feeds back to ICCs to generate/maintain their periodic rhythm.
evidence: The results section provides interpretation of blebbistatin experiment results with acknowledgment of alternative explanations.

claim: Organoidal contractions were completely ceased by 1 μM Nifedipine and resumed after washout, at least partly.
source: Organoidal contractions were completely ceased by 1 μM Nifedipine and resumed after washout, at least partly (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: The results section describes Nifedipine experiment results.

claim: In Nifedipine-treated organoids, Ca2+ transients (GCaMP) in ICCs were erased, which resumed following washout.
source: In Nifedipine-treated organoids, Ca2+ transients (GCaMP) in ICCs were erased, which resumed following washout (Figure 7C).
evidence: The results section describes Ca2+ imaging results after Nifedipine treatment.

claim: Organoids easily fuse to each other.
source: During analyses with our novel organoids, we noticed that they easily fuse to each other, suggesting that organoids grow by progressive fusion (Figure 8A, Figure 8—video 1).
evidence: The results section describes observation of organoid fusion behavior.

claim: Before fusion, Ca2+ oscillatory rhythm was out of phase in two organoids.
source: Before the fusion, Ca2+ oscillatory rhythm was indeed out of phase in the two organoids (Figure 8B, Figure 8—video 2).
evidence: The results section describes Ca2+ imaging results before organoid fusion.

claim: Upon fusion by 24 hr, the rhythm of two organoids became in phase/synchronous.
source: Markedly, upon fusion by 24 hr, their rhythm became in phase/synchronous (Figure 8B, Figure 8—video 2).
evidence: The results section describes Ca2+ imaging results after organoid fusion.

claim: Organoids underwent a 'pause' of oscillation during fusion.
source: Intriguingly, they underwent a 'pause' of oscillation during fusion (see Discussion).
evidence: The results section describes observation of pause during fusion.

claim: After 72 hr of placement of organoids in three-well hydrogel with channels, cellular processes as well as several cell bodies were present within the channel, and Ca2+ transients became synchronized among the three organoids.
source: After 72 hr of placement of organoids, cellular processes as well as several cell bodies were present within the channel, and Ca2+ transients became synchronized among the three organoids (Figure 9C, Figure 9—video 1).
evidence: The results section describes observations from three-well hydrogel experiment.

claim: Organoid-derived cells crawled out from the wells to cover the top surface of the hydrogel, connecting the three organoids.
source: However, with careful examination, we also noticed that organoid-derived cells crawled out from the wells to cover the top surface of the hydrogel, connecting the three organoids (Figure 9D).
evidence: The results section describes observation of cell migration on hydrogel surface.

claim: The surface-covering cells were SMCs (αSMA-positive, c-Kit-negative).
source: By 3 days of culture, the top surface of the hydrogel was indeed covered by cells in a similar way to Figure 9D. These cells were positive for αSMA but negative for c-Kit (Figure 9F), showing that they were SMCs that were somehow detached and crawled out from the peripheral layer of their 'host' organoids.
evidence: The results section describes immunostaining identification of surface cells.

claim: The three organoids in the disconnected wells displayed synchronized Ca2+ transients, coinciding with the top coverage by the SMCs.
source: Importantly, coinciding with the top coverage by the SMCs, the three organoids in the disconnected wells displayed synchronized Ca2+ transients, highlighting the role of SMCs in mediating coordination between organoids (Figure 9G, Figure 9—video 2).
evidence: The results section describes Ca2+ imaging results in disconnected wells.

claim: Gap junction inhibitor yielded no/little effects on the Ca2+ transient coordination in the disconnected well system.
source: Gap junction inhibitor yielded no/little effects on the Ca2+ transient coordination (Figure 9H, Figure 9—video 3).
evidence: The results section describes pharmacological experiment results in the disconnected well system.

claim: The gut contractile organoid displays several unique characteristics including recurrent contractions, maintained differentiation states of ICCs and SMCs, composition essentially of ICCs and SMCs with few ENS cells, and spatial distinction of ICCs and SMCs in living organoids.
source: We have developed a novel gut contractile organoid, which displays several unique characteristics: (1) it undergoes recurrent contractions, (2) differentiation states of ICCs (c-Kit+/αSMA-) and SMCs (c-Kit-/αSMA+) are maintained at least until day 7 in the organoid, (3) the organoid is composed essentially of two types of cells, ICCs and SMCs, with few ENS cells, if any, (4) ICCs (internal) and SMCs (peripheral) can be distinguished for their localization in a living organoid
evidence: The discussion summarizes the key characteristics of the developed organoid.

claim: The gut contractile organoid is composed of a minimum number of cell types that suffice the generation and/or maintenance of rhythmic contractions.
source: Contrasting with many cases in organoid studies that aim at a maximum recapitulation of the intact organ, our gut contractile organoid is composed of a (probably) minimum number of cell types that suffice the generation and/or maintenance of rhythmic contractions, allowing high-resolution analyses at the cellular level.
evidence: The discussion provides interpretation of the organoid's composition.

claim: A peak of Ca2+ transient in ICCs precedes that of SMCs with a latency of 700 msec, implying a signaling from ICC to SMC.
source: Notably, a peak of Ca2+ transient in ICCs precedes that of SMCs with a time lag (also called latency) of 700 msec, implying a signaling from ICC to SMC.
evidence: The discussion interprets the temporal relationship between ICC and SMC Ca2+ peaks.

claim: In a previous study using ICC- and SMC-specific transgenic mice, the rise of GCaMP signal (ICC) preceded that of RCaMP (SMC) with a latency of 56+/-14 ms.
source: These observations are consistent with previous studies using ICC- and SMC-specific transgenic mice that expressed GCaMP and RCaMP, respectively (Baker et al., 2021). In that study, the authors assessed Ca2+ transients in submucosal ICCs (ICC-SM) and compared them with those in their adjacent circular muscles and showed that the rise of GCaMP signal (ICC) preceded that of RCaMP (SMC) with a latency of 56+/-14 ms.
evidence: The discussion cites a previous study for comparison.

claim: Effects by the block of gap junction by CBX or 18β-GA were relatively limited in organoid assays: organoidal contraction rhythm and synchronous patterns of Ca2+ transients remained unchanged between SMC-SMC and ICC-ICC.
source: Effects by the block of gap junction by CBX or 18β-GA were relatively limited in our organoid assays: organoidal contraction rhythm and synchronous patterns of Ca2+ transients remained unchanged between SMC-SMC and ICC-ICC.
evidence: The discussion summarizes the gap junction inhibitor results.

claim: Signaling from ICCs to SMCs was affected by gap junction inhibitors, in which the preceding peak of Ca2+ transient in ICCs was abolished.
source: In contrast, signaling from ICCs to SMCs was affected, in which the preceding peak of Ca2+ transient in ICCs was abolished.
evidence: The discussion summarizes the specific effect of gap junction inhibitors on ICC-SMC signaling.

claim: The contribution of gap junctions to ICC-SMC interactions has been under debate, with some studies reporting that CBX or 18β-GA failed to inhibit these interactions or peristaltic motilities.
source: However, interpretation of the role of gap junction in ICC-SMC interactions, in general, has been under big debate. Some studies reported that CBX or 18β-GA failed to inhibit these interactions or peristaltic motilities (Komuro et al., 1996; Rohr et al., 1998; Schultz et al., 2003)
evidence: The discussion cites studies showing conflicting results about gap junction roles.

claim: Electron microscopy did not detect structures of gap junction in longitudinal muscles in some studies.
source: or that electron microscopy did not detect structures of gap junction in longitudinal muscles (Cousins et al., 2003; Daniel and Wang, 1999; Gabella and Blundell, 1981).
evidence: The discussion cites studies that did not find gap junction structures.

claim: The contribution of gap junctions to the gut motility appears to be highly variable in different regions of the gastrointestinal tract.
source: The contribution of gap junctions to the gut motility appears to be highly variable in different regions of the gastrointestinal tract, for example, stomach versus colon (Iino et al., 2007; Yang et al., 2012).
evidence: The discussion cites studies showing regional variation in gap junction contribution.

claim: While gap junctions are important for the onset of rhythm coordination, once the rhythm is established, other mechanisms might be employed, for example, mechanical feedback from muscles to ICCs.
source: One possibility is that while gap junctions are important for the onset of rhythm coordination, once the rhythm is established, other mechanisms might be employed, for example, mechanical feedback from muscles to ICCs (see below).
evidence: The discussion proposes a speculative mechanism for rhythm coordination.

claim: A similar notion of alternative mechanisms after establishment has been shown for coordinated Ca2+ signaling in cardiac muscle cells.
source: A similar notion has recently been shown for coordinated Ca2+ signaling in cardiac muscle cells (Fukui et al., 2021).
evidence: The discussion cites a study in cardiac muscle cells for comparison.

claim: Thick myosin fibers necessary for the contraction are found only in SMCs but not in ICCs.
source: Since it has been reported that thick myosin fibers necessary for the contraction are found only in SMCs but not in ICCs (Gherghiceanu and Popescu, 2005; Rumessen and Thuneberg, 1991; Rumessen and Thuneberg, 1996; Sun et al., 2006), it is likely that ICCs do not have contractile ability.
evidence: The discussion cites studies on myosin fiber distribution.

claim: ICCs do not have contractile ability.
source: Since it has been reported that thick myosin fibers necessary for the contraction are found only in SMCs but not in ICCs (Gherghiceanu and Popescu, 2005; Rumessen and Thuneberg, 1991; Rumessen and Thuneberg, 1996; Sun et al., 2006), it is likely that ICCs do not have contractile ability.
evidence: The discussion provides inference based on cited structural studies.

claim: ICC's pace-making activity requires mechanical feedback from contracting SMCs.
source: Our observations, therefore, raise the possibility that ICC's pace-making activity requires mechanical feedback from contracting SMCs.
evidence: The discussion proposes a mechanism based on blebbistatin experiment results.

claim: Nifedipine is an L-type Ca2+ channel blocker known to be expressed in SMCs.
source: This notion is also supported by additional findings that Nifedipine, an L-type Ca2+ channel blocker known to be expressed in SMCs (Chevalier et al., 2024; Der et al., 2000; Der-Silaphet et al., 1998), erases both organoidal contractions and Ca2+ transients in ICCs (Figure 7).
evidence: The discussion cites studies on Nifedipine's target.

claim: Reciprocal interactions between pace-making cells and their effectors have been reported in studies of neural circuit establishment.
source: It is of note that the reciprocal interactions between pace-making cells and their effectors have been reported in studies of neural circuit establishment.
evidence: The discussion introduces a parallel from neural circuit studies.

claim: Spontaneous activities emerging in motor neurons during peristaltic locomotion of larvae in Drosophila are regulated by feedback from their governing muscle's contractions.
source: Spontaneous activities emerging in motor neurons during peristaltic locomotion of larvae in Drosophila are regulated by feedback from their governing muscle's contractions, so that motor neurons get organized to display coordinated and stable oscillatory activities (Zeng et al., 2021).
evidence: The discussion cites a study on Drosophila motor neuron feedback.

claim: During early gut peristalsis, ICCs that have initiated their spontaneous activities receive feedback from their governing SMCs to generate more stable coordination of pace-making activity among ICCs.
source: Thus, it is tempting to speculate that during early gut peristalsis, ICCs that have initiated their spontaneous activities receive feedback from their governing SMCs to generate more stable coordination of pace-making activity among ICCs.
evidence: The discussion proposes a speculative mechanism for ICC coordination.

claim: In the very early embryonic gut, origins of peristaltic wave (OPWs) are randomly distributed along the gut axis, but these unstable OPWs later become confined to specific sites displaying more stable and coordinated pace-making patterns.
source: Indeed, we have previously reported that in the very early embryonic gut, origins of peristaltic wave (OPWs) are randomly distributed along the gut axis, but these unstable OPWs later become confined to specific sites displaying more stable and coordinated pace-making patterns (Shikaya et al., 2022).
evidence: The discussion cites the authors' previous study.

claim: In the organoid, the central cells are ICC-MY, and the peripherally lining ones are ICC-IM.
source: Based on the knowledge obtained in studies with mammalian species that ICC-MY are multipolar whereas ICC-IM are bipolar and tightly associated with adjacent SMCs (Huizinga et al., 2011; Iino and Horiguchi, 2006), it is conceivable in our organoids that the central cells are ICC-MY, and the peripherally lining ones are ICC-IM.
evidence: The discussion provides inference based on cited morphological characteristics.

claim: In mice, signaling from ICC-IM to SMCs is gap junction-dependent.
source: In addition, it has been reported in mice that signaling from ICC-IM to SMCs is gap junction-dependent.
evidence: The discussion cites knowledge from mouse studies.

claim: Gap junction-dependent signal found between ICC (central ICC) and SMC in the organoid could be interpreted as ICC-MY (central) signaling to ICC-IM (second-most peripheral), which in turn acts on the external SMCs mediated partly by gap junction.
source: Collectively, our observations that gap junction-dependent signal found between ICC (central ICC) and SMC in the organoid (Figure 5C and D) could be interpreted as follows: ICC-MY (central) signals to ICC-IM (second-most peripheral), which in turn acts on the external SMCs mediated partly by gap junction.
evidence: The discussion provides interpretation of the signaling pathway.

claim: Sequences of signaling (ICC-MY to ICC-IM to SMCs) have been proposed in the intact gut in mammals, although rigid evidence has not been known.
source: Such sequences of signaling (ICC-MY to ICC-IM to SMCs) have also been proposed in the intact gut in mammals, although rigid evidence has not been known.
evidence: The discussion references proposed but unproven signaling sequences.

claim: Two organoids with different oscillatory rhythms eventually coordinate their phases upon fusion.
source: Exploiting the finding obtained in the current study that multiple organoids easily fuse each other in vitro, we have found that two organoids with different oscillatory rhythms eventually coordinate their phases upon the fusion (Figure 8).
evidence: The discussion summarizes the organoid fusion results.

claim: ICCs have the ability to adjust their rhythm to their neighbors.
source: This suggests the ability of ICCs to adjust their rhythm to their neighbors.
evidence: The discussion provides inference from fusion experiment results.

claim: During 'pausing time' of oscillation upon organoidal fusion, organoids might communicate with each other to adjust to a unified rhythm.
source: It is tempting to speculate that during 'pausing time' of oscillation upon organoidal fusion (Figure 8B), they might communicate with each other to adjust to a unified rhythm.
evidence: The discussion proposes a speculative mechanism for rhythm adjustment.

claim: SMCs that crawled out from the organoids and covered the top surface of the hydrogel were able to mediate the rhythm coordination among organoids.
source: During the identification of the rhythm-adjustment mediators using the three-well hydrogel (without connecting channels), SMCs that were unexpectedly crawled out from the organoids and covered the top surface of the hydrogel were able to mediate the rhythm coordination among organoids (Figure 9).
evidence: The discussion summarizes the hydrogel experiment results.

claim: The findings have revealed a novel role of SMCs in mediating rhythm coordination.
source: Nevertheless, our findings have revealed a novel role of SMCs in mediating rhythm coordination, and as discussed above, these support the notion of the SMC-to-ICC signaling, which is unprecedented.
evidence: The discussion provides interpretation of the novel finding.

claim: Gap junctions do not play a major role in SMC-mediated organoidal phase synchronization.
source: It is unlikely that gap junctions play a major role in such signaling since gap junction inhibitors yielded no detectable effects in SMC-mediated organoidal phase synchronization (Figure 9H).
evidence: The discussion provides inference from pharmacological experiment results.
